title: Internal Hom versus pullback for a site-perfect first variable
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $g:Y'\to X$ be a
morphism of finite-type schemes,
let $M$ be a site-perfect complex
in $D(X,A)$, and let $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ belong to the
finite-Tor constructible category.
The canonical comparison for
derived pullback and internal Hom
is an isomorphism

$$
Lg^*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\mathcal Hom_A(Lg^*M,Lg^*N).
$$

It is natural in both variables and compatible with shifts and
distinguished triangles in $N$.

proof.text:
Work on small skeletons of the coefficient sites and put $H_X(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_A(U,V)$, $\mathbf1_X=A_X$, and $F=Lg^*$. The finite-level operations are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] the ambient categories are closed symmetric monoidal, with $H_X(M,-)$ right adjoint to $-\otimes^L M$ and evaluation as counit. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], $F$ is strong symmetric monoidal with its canonical tensor comparison and $F\mathbf1_X\cong\mathbf1_{Y'}$. Define $\beta_{M,N}$ to be the transpose of
$$FH_X(M,N)\otimes FM\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H_X(M,N)\otimes M)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev})}FN.$$
This specifies the canonical comparison, including its normalization; no arbitrary isomorphism between the two objects is substituted.

source.place: Proof, finite-perfect dual evaluation and pullback of evaluation; expanded using the proof of sk-thm-sf-internal-hom-pullback in the same unit

proof.text:
Set $D=H_X(M,\mathbf1_X)$ and let $e=\mathrm{ev}_{M,\mathbf1_X}:D\otimes M\to\mathbf1_X$ be coefficient evaluation. Site-perfectness [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] is local bounded finite-projective perfectness on this ringed site (a covering of the final object pulls back to every object, and restrictions of direct summands of finite free modules are such), so [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] applies, for every ambient second variable $T$: its canonical evaluation comparison, written with the factors as in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_T=e_{M,T}:T\otimes D\xrightarrow{\sim}H_X(M,T).$$
By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], $\theta_T$ is internal composition $H_X(\mathbf1_X,T)\otimes H_X(M,\mathbf1_X)\to H_X(M,T)$ after $T\cong H_X(\mathbf1_X,T)$, and internal composition is the transpose of the composite evaluation [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Hence $\mathrm{ev}_{M,T}\circ(\theta_T\otimes1_M)=1_T\otimes e$ (unitor understood); on representatives $y\otimes\phi\otimes x\mapsto y\,\phi(x)$. The closed adjunction of step 1 followed by $\theta_T^{-1}$ gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(S\otimes M,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,T\otimes D)$ natural in $S,T$, i.e. an adjunction $-\otimes M\dashv-\otimes D$ with counit $1_T\otimes e$. Let $c:\mathbf1_X\to M\otimes D$ be its unit at $\mathbf1_X$. The triangle identity at $\mathbf1_X$ is the first identity below. Then $1_T\otimes c$ is the unit at $T$: under the counit it transposes to $1_T\otimes(1_M\otimes e)(c\otimes1_M)=1_{T\otimes M}$, and the unit is the unique arrow with this transpose. The other triangle identity at $\mathbf1_X$, with unit $1_D\otimes c$ at $D$ and counit $e$ at $\mathbf1_X$, is the second:
$$(1_M\otimes e)(c\otimes1_M)=1_M,\qquad(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes c)=1_D,$$
with associators and unitors understood. Thus $(D,M,e,c)$ is an actual dual pair, obtained from the finite-perfect evaluation isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, finite-perfect dual evaluation and pullback of evaluation; expanded using the proof of sk-thm-sf-internal-hom-pullback in the same unit

proof.text:
Apply $F$ to both displayed identities. Define $e':FD\otimes FM\to\mathbf1_{Y'}$ by the inverse tensor comparison, $F(e)$ and the unit comparison; define $c':\mathbf1_{Y'}\to FM\otimes FD$ by the inverse unit comparison, $F(c)$ and the tensor comparison. The associativity and unit coherence in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identifies the images of the two identities with
$$(1_{FM}\otimes e')(c'\otimes1_{FM})=1_{FM},\qquad(e'\otimes1_{FD})(1_{FD}\otimes c')=1_{FD}.$$
So $(FD,FM,e',c')$ is a dual pair. This step applies a functor to equations and substitutes its coherent tensor and unit identifications.

source.place: Proof, finite-perfect dual evaluation and pullback of evaluation; expanded using the proof of sk-thm-sf-internal-hom-pullback in the same unit

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions] to the dual pair of step 3: it gives $-\otimes FM\dashv-\otimes FD$. Its bijection is the explicit one (Mathlib tensorRightHomEquiv, Rigid/Basic.lean): $w:T\otimes FM\to V$ goes to $(w\otimes1_{FD})(1_T\otimes c')$, with inverse $u\mapsto(1_V\otimes e')(u\otimes1_{FM})$; the two composites are identities by the two triangle identities of step 3 and an interchange of independent factors, so this is checked here and not taken from the node statement. Its counit is therefore $1_V\otimes e'$. Compare it with $-\otimes FM\dashv H_{Y'}(FM,-)$ from [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Let
$$\theta'_V:V\otimes FD\longrightarrow H_{Y'}(FM,V)$$
be the transpose of $1_V\otimes e'$ under the closed adjunction, and $\psi_V:H_{Y'}(FM,V)\to V\otimes FD$ the arrow corresponding to $\mathrm{ev}_{FM,V}$ under the explicit bijection. Both adjunction bijections represent the functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes FM,V)$; $\theta'_V\psi_V$ and $\psi_V\theta'_V$ correspond to $\mathrm{ev}_{FM,V}$ and to $1_V\otimes e'$ under these bijections, as do the identities, so both composites are identities and $\theta'_V$ is invertible. Naturality in $V$ follows from the naturality of both bijections.

source.place: Proof, finite-perfect dual evaluation and pullback of evaluation; expanded using the proof of sk-thm-sf-internal-hom-pullback in the same unit

proof.text:
Form the composite of isomorphisms
$$FH_X(M,N)\xrightarrow{F(\theta_N^{-1})}F(N\otimes D)\xrightarrow{\sim}FN\otimes FD\xrightarrow{\theta'_{FN}}H_{Y'}(FM,FN).$$
Its transpose is $F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})$ after the inverse tensor comparison: by step 2, evaluation after $\theta_N\otimes1_M$ is $1_N\otimes e$; by step 4, evaluation after $\theta'_{FN}\otimes1_{FM}$ is $1_{FN}\otimes e'$; step 3 identifies the latter with $F(1_N\otimes e)$ through the tensor comparison. Cancelling $F\theta_N$ in this equality gives exactly the transpose used to define $\beta_{M,N}$ in step 1. Injectivity of the closed adjunction bijection shows that the composite equals $\beta_{M,N}$. Hence the canonical comparison is invertible.

source.place: Proof, finite-perfect dual evaluation and pullback of evaluation; expanded using the proof of sk-thm-sf-internal-hom-pullback in the same unit

proof.text:
Naturality holds also for noninvertible maps of site-perfect first variables. For $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$, the defining counit identity
$$\mathrm{ev}_{M',N'}\circ(H_X(a,b)\otimes1_{M'})=b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(1\otimes a)$$
is naturality of evaluation in the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Applying $F$, using the bifunctorial tensor comparison, and transposing gives the naturality square for $\beta$. For shifts and triangles use the exact derived pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and the shift and triangle structures on internal Hom of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The comparison preserves their specified shift structures, as can be checked on the representative evaluation of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]: a homogeneous family $f$ evaluates on $x$ to $f(x)$, and the Hom differential is $d_Nf-(-1)^{|f|}fd_M$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Shifting $N$ changes $d_N$ by the same sign on both sides. For a shift of the first variable, the identification $H(M[1],N)\cong H(M,N)[-1]$ sends a degree-$r$ homogeneous map to $(-1)^r$ times its reindexed family; substituting $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$ in the displayed differential verifies this sign, and $F$ preserves it. Finally, evaluating into a cone acts componentwise on its $N_2\oplus N_1[1]$ terms, so commutes with the inclusion, projection, and cone differential matrix. These identities pass through the normalized representative comparison to the derived category. Thus $\beta$ is a transformation of exact functors in $N$ and gives a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the connecting arrow. Restrict this ambient conclusion to the stated $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
